title: Foreign Acquisitions and Takeovers Fees Imposition Amendment (Near-new Dwelling Interests) Bill 2018
short_title: Foreign Acquisitions and Takeovers Fees Imposition Amendment (Near-new Dwelling Interests) Bill 2018

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would impose fees payable by developers when near-new dwellings were sold to foreign buyers under the relevant exemption certificates for those sales.
It would amend foreign investment fee legislation to support reconciliation payments for these transactions, covering dwellings whose earlier sales had failed to reach settlement.
It would accompany a broader housing tax bill establishing the reconciliation mechanism, with developers paying fees for covered sales rather than buyers lodging individual applications.
changes: The fee amendments would apply retrospectively from 1 July 2017 to sales made under near-new dwelling exemption certificates.
Developers holding certificates issued at least six months before enactment would have a 12-month initial reconciliation period.
Related wording and notes in the fee legislation would be updated to accommodate the new charges.
summary.affected: Property developers selling near-new dwellings to foreign persons under near-new dwelling exemption certificates would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Matt Thistlethwaite
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the government's housing affordability bills do not address the core problems of negative gearing and the 50% capital gains tax discount, which primarily benefit high-income earners and inflate house prices. Labor's alternative policies would restrict negative gearing to new properties only and reduce the capital gains tax discount to 25%, aiming to reduce competition for first home buyers and increase housing supply.
